nodes.label: CompressionConfig
nodes.rationale: Three modes only — none, gzip, zstd; there is deliberately no brotli or deflate. Level is algorithm-specific and out-of-range values are clamped.

nodes.label: zstd compression
nodes.rationale: Best ratio at competitive speed and very fast decode at every level, which makes it a strong default for read-heavy state. Writing requires native support (Bun or Node); there is no pure-JS fallback for compression.

nodes.label: gzip compression
nodes.rationale: The store default because it needs no native runtime support and no extra dependency — node:zlib works on Bun, Node and Deno alike.

nodes.label: ATS1 body manifest header
nodes.rationale: Every body carries a small ATS1 manifest whose flags byte records the compression algorithm (and the encryption/key-version/binding bits). Decoding is driven entirely by that flag, never by an HTTP header — on S3 Content-Encoding is set only as a courtesy marker. Because each body self-describes, none/gzip/zstd bodies mix freely in one bucket.

nodes.label: Decompression cap (bomb protection)
nodes.rationale: Read output is bounded to 512 MiB by default so a few KB inflating to many GB cannot exhaust memory during recovery. gzip and zstd hand the bound to the decoder via zlib's maxOutputLength, refusing an over-cap body before its output is allocated; the two paths that cannot take the option (Bun's zstdDecompressSync and the fzstd fallback) only assert the decoded size afterwards, so there the bound is a correctness check rather than bomb protection. Raise it with withMaxDecompressedBytes.

nodes.label: Compress before encrypt
nodes.rationale: Compressing ciphertext is pointless because it is high-entropy, and the fixed order also avoids CRIME-style side channels. Setting both options gets this order automatically.

nodes.label: fzstd decompress-only fallback
nodes.rationale: The optional fzstd peer dependency lets a runtime without native zstd READ zstd bodies written elsewhere, but it caps the back-reference window at 32 MB, so ultra levels (>= 20) may be unreadable there. Keep the level <= 19 if any reader in the fleet might lack native zstd.

nodes.label: Level is an encoder-only setting
nodes.rationale: The manifest records the algorithm, not the level, and gzip and zstd frames are self-describing — so changing the configured level needs no migration and old and new bodies mix freely.

nodes.label: Detect zstd by calling it, not by feature-checking
nodes.rationale: Deno's node:zlib exports zstd entry points with no binding behind them, so a presence check would pass and then fail cryptically. Both directions pick an implementation by calling it, which keeps the framework's own capability message accurate and leaves the fzstd fallback reachable.
